\[
\hat{d}(n) = \mathbf{w}(n)^{\top} \mathbf{x}(n),\quad e(n) = d(n) - \hat{d}(n),\quad
\mathbf{w}(n+1) = \mathbf{w}(n) + \frac{\mu\, e(n)\, \mathbf{x}(n)}{\varepsilon + \mathbf{x}(n)^{\top} \mathbf{x}(n)}
\]

The formula shows the default parameter values.

where

- \(d(n)\): The pixel, from 0 to 1
- \(\mathbf{x}(n)\): Its neighbors in the window, without the center
- \(\mathbf{w}(n)\): The weights at pixel n
- \(e(n)\): The prediction error
- \(\mu\): The step size

n runs over the pixels in raster order. d is the pixel, scaled to 0 to 1. x holds its neighbors in the window without the center. The weights w start as the plain mean of the neighbors. After each pixel they move by the error e times x. Hadhoud and Thomas brought this LMS update to two dimensions. Here the step is divided by the energy of x, as in normalized LMS. That is our choice, so that one step size suits any image. A tiny epsilon avoids a division by zero.
